one_line_description.value: Commas (formerly FanBasis) is a creator-commerce platform for creating, selling and getting paid, combining courses, communities, webinars, affiliate tooling and built-in payments.
one_line_description.quote: One place to create, sell, and get paid, with payments built in.

has_public_api.quote: Embedded checkouts, multi-rail payouts, APIs and SDKs.

api_type.quote: Make a POST request to `https://www.fanbasis.com/public-api/checkout-sessions` with your product name, price, and type.

api_breadth.value: REST public API covering checkout sessions, payments/transactions, subscriptions, customers, discounts, invoices and webhooks; read-write
api_breadth.quote: Everything you need to collect payments, manage subscriptions, reward customers, and automate your business with Commas.

auth_methods.quote: Log into your Commas dashboard and go to Account → API Keys.

access_model.quote: Sign in to access API Docs

access_notes.value: The official API reference at dev-docs.fanbasis.com is behind a password login, so the developer-onboarding path is not publicly readable. Keys are created inside the merchant dashboard (production) and inside a separate sandbox dashboard (sandbox.commas.net) for test keys; no public pricing/plan evidence shows whether a paid plan, approval step, or sales contact is required first. API detail evidence comes from commasdocs.com and an npm CLI package flagged non-official in this bundle (the CLI author email is @fanbasis.com).
access_notes.quote: Create production keys in your Commas dashboard and sandbox keys in the sandbox dashboard, both under Account → API Keys

official_mcp_server.quote: Commas CLI — run your Commas (formerly FanBasis) business from the terminal, powered by the Commas MCP server

webhooks.quote: Set up a webhook subscription so Commas notifies your server the moment `payment.succeeded` fires.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: The sandbox is `https://api-sandbox.commas.net` and needs its own API key, created in the sandbox dashboard at https://sandbox.commas.net (Account → API Keys).

verdict_reason: Commas (formerly FanBasis) has a REST public API for checkout sessions, payments, subscriptions, customers and webhooks, plus a separate sandbox environment and a vendor CLI backed by a Commas MCP server. The catch is distribution: the official developer docs at dev-docs.fanbasis.com are password-gated and no public pricing or plan page documents how an outside developer obtains API access. With access terms unconfirmed and no Composio toolkit, this is moderate rather than easy.
main_blocker: Official API docs are password-gated; access/plan terms are not public
open_questions: FanBasis appears to have rebranded to Commas (per multiple third-party sources in the search snippets); confirm whether fanbasis.com/public-api endpoints and dev-docs.fanbasis.com are still the current, supported surface or are being migrated to commasdocs.com.

Is the password for dev-docs.fanbasis.com (official API docs) issued automatically to Commas merchants, or must it be requested from FanBasis/Commas support? This decides whether access is self-serve or approval-based.
Which plan tier includes API/SDK access, and is a paid plan or sales conversation required before production keys can be created? No pricing page content was captured that states this.

Official SDK languages are unconfirmed: a search snippet describes @fanbasis/checkout-sdk as 'The official TypeScript library for the Fanbasis Checkout API', but that page was not captured as a source; the marketing site only says 'APIs and SDKs'.
Rate limits/quotas are not documented in any captured source.
No OAuth or scope documentation was found; evidence indicates API-key-only authentication. Confirm there is no OAuth flow.
The Commas MCP server endpoint URL is not published anywhere in the captured evidence; only the vendor CLI (thin client to the MCP server) documents its behaviour.
No community/third-party MCP servers for FanBasis/Commas were surfaced by the searches.
API versioning/deprecation policy was not found; the docs site title references 'API Docsv3', which may indicate a v3 API.
